claims.statement: Modules/billing splits billing into two readiness signals that must stay separate: `isBillingReady` is threshold-only (ongoing AND ≥ BILLING_READY_THRESHOLD 80) and is the alert/badge prep signal, while `billingGate` adds the requirement that all required supporting documents are on file and is the generate-gate the queue enforces.

`billingGate` reports `docsVerified: false` whenever the requirement catalog is empty (`requiredTotal > 0` guard), so an unevaluated checklist never reads as ready; the test file pins that case alongside the three threshold/document combinations.

`isBillingReady` re-requires `status === 'ongoing'`, so a completed batch is never gate-ready even at 100% progress with every document verified; `buildBillingCards` filters completed batches out so only a direct caller meets the case.

`modules/billing/domain/rates.ts` holds current rates only (no circular or effectivity columns) because ADR-001 BB1-prune puts version safety in the batch snapshot, and its qualification lookups fall back silently to 360 nominal hours and ₱15,000 for an unmapped qualification.
`tracksForProgram` always returns Training Cost and TSF/Allowance and appends Entrepreneurship only for CFSP, so a TWSP batch has no Entrepreneurship track at all (PAFSE routes it out of scope).

`buildStatement` is the pure document engine per track: Training Cost is the flat per-qualification cost, TSF is `tsfDaysFor(qualification) × ₱160` plus CFSP-only New Normal ₱1,000 and Insurance ₱100.80, Entrepreneurship is ₱800, and each is multiplied by the roster length.
The statement's TSF cover title drops the New Normal claim for a TWSP batch, reading "Training Support Fund (TSF)" instead of the CFSP title.

`buildStatement` tolerates a missing roster (`batch.scholars_list ?? []`) by emitting a zero-row table and a zero total, and `scholars_list` is not part of the batches snapshot — only the report route attaches it, and that fetch is already ordered by last_name, first_name, id, which satisfies ADR-001 Order.

Not implemented in the statement builder: the FF2 absence deduction on the final tranche, the Flag-3x exclusion of dual-trained scholars from the ₱800 entrepreneurship fee, tranche percentages, and signatory/letterhead/addressee population from `tenant_settings`.
`pesosInWords` renders the cover amount in words including an `/100` centavo tail, and collapses a negative or non-finite amount to "Zero Pesos only" instead of a malformed string.

Per ADR-003 P1 a packet is a projection of `(batch_id, billing_type, tranche_no)`, not an entity, and `packets.ts` currently implements only the batch axis: `buildPackets` emits one packet per batch and the `PKT-NNN` ref is a display-only sequence.

`buildPacket` derives state rather than reading it: `settled` for a completed batch, `ready` when there are no blockers, else `draft`; only draft, ready and settled are ever produced, so `generated`/`submitted` are never emitted.
Packet blockers cover sub-80% progress, unsatisfied supporting documents, and an unavailable requirement catalog (reported separately so an empty catalog never reads as satisfied).

`PRE_BILLING_STAGES` deliberately excludes `assess` and `bill` stage documents because billing produces those, so requiring them would make readiness circular and leave Generate permanently dead; `data/billing.ts` mirrors the set and additionally requires `critical`.

Both billing gates read document state through `isDocOnFile`, which under ADR-004 D4 treats an untracked requirement as not satisfied while accepting `submitted` (ADR-001 §7.2.4 accepts an uploaded attendance sheet), so only pending, missing and untracked hold a packet back.
A packet accepts a free-text search over ref, batch name, qualification, school code and program, case-insensitively.

Packet due dates are derived on read (`daysToDue` = `batch.daysToBilling`, overdue = live and negative) with nothing stored, and ADR-008 BD5 leaves the packet due date derived while its recorded `batches.billing_deadline` covers only the batch-level commitment.

Because the mapper computes `daysToBilling` from a null deadline as the `Infinity` sentinel, a batch with no recorded deadline yields `daysToDue: Infinity` and the literal due label "Due in Infinityd".

Nothing in the module writes packet state: `submitted` and `settled` are user-asserted marks (ADR-003 P3), only `generated` would write the append-only `billing_records` snapshot, and closing the preview explicitly toasts that nothing was saved.

The `billing_records` RLS policies grant SELECT to an explicit admin/coordinator/viewer allowlist (deliberately not `can_read_batch`, which would admit trainers) and INSERT only to `can_manage_tenant`, with no UPDATE or DELETE policy, making the log append-only in the database.
`billing_type` and the Assessment Fee: the migration mirrors `BillingTrackId` exactly and omits the assessment fee by design per ADR-001 TVI-scope.
`deriveDocReadiness` counts only `critical` requirements in the four pre-billing stages, so the generate-gate denominator is narrower than the whole catalog.
`resolveTenant` is called with an empty tenant list, so the statement cover prints the raw tenant UUID as the school name (a rule 6 ID leak) and leaves the region blank.

`app/(dashboard)/t/[tenantCode]/(sections)/billing/page.tsx` redirects a trusted trainer to `/trainer` on `resolveTrustedRole` before any batch fetch, and only afterwards derives the render role via `toOfficeRole(resolveRouteRole(...))` with a `viewer` least-privilege fallback — presentation only, so a real trainer adding `?role=admin` still lands on `/trainer`.
The route's `syncFailed && batches.length === 0` guard returns the retry state before the empty state, keeping a failed fetch from reading as an empty queue (rule 19).
The queue's `canWrite` only hides controls; RLS is the boundary, and the route already refuses trainers.
The queue builds packets and preview cards from an empty requirement catalog and an empty school-code map, degrading to an unresolved school code and a closed gate rather than a fabricated pass.
The activity, and `billing_readiness` signups, only one direct test file: `tests/unit/billing-readiness.test.ts`.
`.docx` population, a real `billing_records` fetch, the 20/50/80 tranche ladder with per-tranche checklists, and FF2 absence deduction are planned but absent from the module.

The route applies preview overrides before the empty guard: `?state=denied` returns its own state, then `syncFailed && batches.length === 0` returns the retry state ahead of the empty and `no-tenant-access` branches (RULES.md rule 19), and only an `ok` non-empty snapshot falls through to BillingQueueView's inline sync-failed banner.

`billingRole` comes from `toOfficeRole(await resolveRouteRole(params, dbRole))` and runs after the trainer redirect, so a real trainer adding `?role=admin` still lands on `/trainer`; any non-office resolved role, including a previewed `trainer`, narrows to read-only `viewer`.
BillingQueueView derives `canWrite` as `role !== 'viewer'`, which hides the Generate and Preview controls and shows a read-only banner for a viewer; RLS remains the boundary.

Both the header's Generate action and the detail panel's Preview action open the statement modal only for a card whose `gate.ready` is true, the header falling back to the first generable card — the packet state chip never decides generability.

The route still passes an empty `documentRequirements` array even though `Batch` now carries document requirements from the embedded `scholarship_programs.program_document_requirements` select, so both the gate and every packet blocker stay closed on live data until billing reads the field.

A packet's due date is derived from the recorded `batches.billing_deadline` (via `daysToBilling`), not from the tranche schedules ADR-003 P5 names; ADR-008 BD5 sanctions this and leaves reconciling the two to a future ADR.

`buildPacket` derives three of the five states only: `settled` when the batch is completed, `ready` when no blockers remain, else `draft`; nothing in the module produces `generated` or `submitted`, and a reload re-derives the state rather than reading a store.

The queue's closing copy is the rule surface: the preview footer reads 'Internal working copy · TESDA SIS and BSRS remain authoritative', and closing the preview toasts that nothing was saved or submitted to TESDA — ADR-003 P3 keeps TESDA authoritative.

The mapper derives `totalDays` from `row.total_sessions ?? 0` as a compatibility alias, so a batch with a null session count yields a ₱0 TSF packet amount (`totalDays × ₱160 × scholars`) even though its statement's training period has a real source; the `documentRequirements` catalog gap is the successor to the TES-34 TODO rather than a missing field.

Screenshot of packets: `buildPackets` sends one packet per batch through `buildPacket`, whose condition set is `pre_billing_stages` (aou/ntp/tip/train), the readiness threshold, and unsatisfied critical pre-billing documents — three packet states are derived only by `batch.status`.
